Name: Improper External Identity Verification
Description:
The product supports user accounts that include a user's external
		identifier or communications channel - such as email, phone number,
		social media account, or domain name - but it does not properly verify
		that the user actually controls the associated identifier or channel.

CommonConsequences.Note: If an external identifier is controlled by an attacker, such as an email address, then the attacker might be able to perform a "pre-hijacking attack" against a victim who creates or recovers their account.

PotentialMitigations.Description: Before changing the contact information, send a message to the user with a confirmation code. Only make the change when the user provides the correct code. Ensure that the confirmation code is expired and rendered invalid if the user does not respond quickly enough.

References.Title: New Research Paper: Pre-hijacking Attacks on Web User Accounts
Pre-hijacked accounts: An Empirical Study of Security Failures in User Account Creation on the Web
NIST SP 800-63C-4: Digital Identity Guidelines: Identity Proofing and Enrollment. Section 3.8. Requirements for Confirmation Codes
